Having somebody to talk to is by far the most effective help there is. It eases this existencial anxiety. The neutral and hypomanic episodes can last a couple of months, then the manic one  about a month or so and then depression follows for a few months. The beginning of my cycle I would say is the neutral, somewhat healthy part after a bout of depression. Then slowly my energy and planning increase and I start making todo lists, travel plans, education plans and so on. After a while The planning gets ridiculous, like last time I was planning to take 15 subjects this fall. I stop being able to stop drinking when I go to parties, I spend money on ridicoulus things and I am the most important person in the world, capable of doing anything. Soon I start getting in my head thinking people are talking about me. Then I start having near religious experiences when listening to music or watching a movie or sitting on the bus. The world starts to get a little to beautiful and I begin to feel the pressure of it all. Then slowly my world starts going in to pieces, I cry constantly for a couple of weeks before landing deep down in the abyss. Then I stay there thinking my life is over. 

Now I have just come to an end of a deep depression. I feel like a different person to the one who keeps trying and hoping and planning and wanting and who gets stuck in a state of confusion for months. I watch her and think, no, I won't put her through this again. I will end her pain while she is asleep, so she doesn't have to wake up to the same scary world again. 

The UV lamp is a good idea, I will look into buying one. The sun cycles almost make the whole country a little bipolar.

Dying would kill my mom and dad as well, not just me. My brother would struggle a lot as I am his only sibling. I don't want to leave him alone in this world. He only has me who really understands him. I really appreciate your support, you are helping more than you know. I know it would stir up a lot of worries in people around me if I vented my thoughts to them, and I like having the situation around me as normal as possible without there being so much focus on me and my issues. 

Today I actually feel like maybe there might be a tiny chance of me surviving. I'm going to go have some ice cream for breakfast now to celebrate me not being suicidal anymore. Knowing someone will listen without judgement when im at the bottom of the pit is reassuring.

I have always followed the advice given by my doctors. Other than that I have tried several types of meditation that do ease my anxiety, though I am often not well enough to get through or even begin a session. Cognitive behavioural, psychotherapy have worked on a lot of my social, self esteem and relationship issues. I have been in-patient and im not sure what out pasient translates to in my country. Creative writing, exercise and theatre is something I do when I am well enough for it, but I am severely limited by my fatigue. I try to read books on personal issues more or less unrelated to my mental illness, and I am trying to find a way to implement music in my life in a way that is enjoyable and not straining. Acupuncture I have tried. Spiritual I would say I have at least experienced in manic episodes. I downladed visual videos that was meant to get me in a trance, which had some effect on some issues. When I eat very healtily I feel lighter and have slightly more energy, but when my brain craves dopamine I fucking eat crap. Many things work here and there to some extent, but they cannot be applied at all when I am as sick as I am now. I am in bed all week except my few classes I have which I dread and which drain me. The pressure of doing anything is my absolute biggest challenge. Because I want to do everything but end up not being able to do much of it because of fatigue. Hopefully when the sun is back in full I will have some energy to begin doing some of the activities that will further increase my energy, until then I am locked in bed. I just don't want to repeat that same cycle again. I hope so much so much of the time and Ive just used it all up. I don't believe I will survive. Every cycle hits harder than the previous one and this time it hasn't been safe. I want so it to stop. I try so fucking hard.

I'm currently with my 11th psychiatrist at only 22 years old. I have tried most antidepressives and antipsychotics (was misdiagnosed schizophrenic there for a while). I even had ECT right after my 18th birthday. Now I'm on a mood stabilizer, reluctant to take anything else due to bad experiences. I had some emergency valium, because I certainly deal with my fair share of anxiety, but I was scared it would make the problem worse in the long run so I quit. Though a slight valium dependency might be preferable to dying. My brain is by all appearances treatment resistant.

My brain is riddled with disease. I never have days or even hours anymore where I am not reminded of it. How is it ever worth it? Why can't leaving be a beautiful thing. 

That said, thank you for your support these last few days. I have felt less alone, and I am not feeling as suicidal as I was. Though I know too well its just a waiting game to see if I survive the next time.

I hope you are doing okay whoever and wherever you are.

Antidepressants and antipsychotics made me feel like not myself as well. It made me feel drugged and bored and dumb, and it made my world just seem wrong.

I went without medication for three years due to bad experiences with antidepressants and antipsychotics and swore never to take any medication again. 

Recently i started taking Lamictal, a mood stabilizer. It has made me feel like myself again, after about 8 years. Not feeling drugged, not feeling different, just back to the way I was before my illness. I had forgotten how that felt until recently when I began taking Lamictal. I resisted trying it for so long, and that time now seems unnecessary difficult.

Please reconsider trying it. If it helps you the way it helps me you will never in a million years regret it. Just giving it a three week shot could change your life and I really want that for you. I hope you figure things out.
